title: Rivian partner Mind Robotics hires Doug Field as president
key_facts: Mind Robotics, a robotics start-up founded in 2025 by Rivian chief executive RJ Scaringe, appointed Doug Field as president.

Field was Ford's EV and software chief until earlier this year, and before that a VP at Apple (Project Titan, the unsuccessful self-driving car effort) and Tesla's chief vehicle engineer on the Model 3.
Mind Robotics says Field will oversee its work on 'universally capable robots' for Rivian's factories and other uses.
The start-up has raised over $1 billion, has not shown any robot in public and has not confirmed whether it is building a humanoid; it has 32 open positions.
A correction on 13 Oct 2026 says Mind Robotics is a partner of Rivian, not a spin-off; Rivian owns equity and will be the first customer, and Mind Robotics uses AI training data from Rivian.
Scaringe is acting CEO and chair of Mind Robotics and says he wants to keep the two companies separate.
quote_evidence: Rivian CEO RJ Scaringe’s startup Mind Robotics announced the appointment of Doug Field as president in a major coup for the CEO’s secretive robotics project.
Correction October 13th: Mind Robotics is a partner of Rivian, but not a spinoff.
While the company has yet to show off any of its robots in public, the startup says its robots are being designed with “dexterity and physical reasoning” that’s required for industrial work.
why_it_matters_hint: A senior car-industry executive takes over a well-funded robot start-up that has shown no robot yet.
event_date: Announcement 13 Oct 2026 (The Verge corrected the Rivian relationship the same day).
notes: The Verge's correction says Mind Robotics is a partner of Rivian and not a spin-off; the wording follows the correction.
